lessons.title: A Roman club takes shape
lessons.subtitle: Discover the city clubs and symbols behind Roma’s identity.

story.title: A club for Rome
story.body: Roma was formed when Fortitudo-ProRoma, Football Club di Roma and Alba-Audace merged in 1927.

story.title: A new emblem and colours
story.body: The Capitoline Wolf and the city colours, yellow and red, gave the new club an identity.

facts.label: Roma founding year
facts.prompt: In what year was Associazione Sportiva Roma formed?
facts.scope: The year AS Roma was formed from three Rome clubs.
facts.evidence: The history states Roma was born in spring 1927 after the merger of the three named clubs.

facts.label: Founding clubs
facts.prompt: Which three clubs merged to form Roma?
answers: Fortitudo-ProRoma, Football Club di Roma and Alba-Audace
distractors: Alba-Audace, Juventus and Football Club di Roma

value.display: Fortitudo-ProRoma, Football Club di Roma and Alba-Audace
value.text: Fortitudo-ProRoma, Football Club di Roma and Alba-Audace

facts.scope: The merger that formed AS Roma in 1927.
facts.evidence: The official history names Fortitudo-ProRoma, Football Club di Roma, and Alba-Audace as the merging clubs.

facts.label: Club symbol
facts.prompt: Which symbol did Roma adopt for its crest at its formation?
facts.scope: Roma’s original club identity described in its official history.
facts.evidence: The club history says the new club took on the Capitoline Wolf symbol for its crest.

lessons.title: The 1984 European Cup final in Rome
lessons.subtitle: A home-city final tested Roma on Europe’s biggest stage.

story.title: Home advantage
story.body: Roma reached the 1984 European Cup final after victories over Göteborg, CSKA Sofia, Dinamo Berlin and Dundee United.

story.title: A final decided on penalties
story.body: Pruzzo cancelled Phil Neal’s opener at the Stadio Olimpico, but Liverpool won the shootout.

facts.label: European Cup final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Roma face in the 1984 European Cup final at the Stadio Olimpico?
facts.scope: The 1984 European Cup final in Rome.
facts.evidence: The official history says Roma faced English champions Liverpool in the European Cup final at the Stadio Olimpico.

facts.label: European Cup final score
facts.prompt: What was the score after extra time in Roma’s 1984 European Cup final against Liverpool?
facts.scope: The final score before the penalty shootout; Liverpool won 4-2 on penalties.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s official season overview records the final as Liverpool 1-1 Roma, with Liverpool winning 4-2 on penalties.

facts.label: Roma’s 1984 European Cup final venue
facts.prompt: At which stadium did Roma host Liverpool in the 1984 European Cup final?
facts.scope: The venue of Roma’s 1984 European Cup final against Liverpool.
facts.evidence: The official history notes Roma enjoyed home advantage at the Stadio Olimpico for the final.

lessons.title: A capital celebrates the Scudetto
lessons.subtitle: A title-winning team leaves its mark on the capital.

story.title: A season-long lead
story.body: Roma finished the 2000-01 campaign with 75 points and secured the title on the final day.

story.title: Three Scudetti
story.body: The championship was Roma’s third league title, after the 1942 and 1983 wins.

facts.label: Roma 2000-01 points
facts.prompt: How many points did Roma collect in its 2000-01 title-winning league season?
facts.scope: Roma’s points total in the completed 2000–01 Serie A season.
facts.evidence: The official history says Roma ended the season with 75 points, then the record for an 18-team championship.

facts.label: Top scorer in Roma title side
facts.prompt: Who scored 20 goals for Roma during the 2000-01 Scudetto season?
facts.scope: Roma’s leading scorer in the 2000-01 title season, as described in the club history.
facts.evidence: The history states Batistuta scored 20 goals and names him among the title-winning heroes.

facts.label: Roma Scudetto count
facts.prompt: The 2000-01 title was which Scudetto in Roma’s history?
facts.scope: The league title Roma secured on 17 June 2001.
facts.evidence: The history section calls this “A third Scudetto” and says the title was won in 2000-01.

lessons.title: From Lodigiani to Roma’s first team
lessons.subtitle: Follow Totti from youth football to his first senior milestones.

story.title: Roma youth pathway
story.body: Totti played youth football at Fortitudo, SMIT Trastevere and Lodigiani before joining Roma.

story.title: A senior debut
story.body: He made his Serie A debut away to Brescia in March 1993, then scored his first league goal against Foggia.

facts.label: Roma registration date
facts.prompt: On what date did Roma register Francesco Totti with the Italian FA?
facts.scope: The date his Roma journey began as a registered youth player.
facts.evidence: The profile states Roma registered Totti with the Italian FA on 20 July 1989.

facts.label: Serie A debut opponent
facts.prompt: Against which club did Totti make his Serie A debut in March 1993?
facts.scope: Totti’s Serie A debut on 28 March 1993.
facts.evidence: The profile says his Serie A debut came against Brescia at Stadio Rigamonti on 28 March.

facts.label: First Serie A goal opponent
facts.prompt: Against which club did Totti score his first Serie A goal on 4 September 1994?
facts.scope: Totti’s first Serie A goal, scored after joining Roma’s first-team preseason.
facts.evidence: The profile states he scored his first Serie A goal against Foggia on 4 September 1994.

lessons.title: A captain in defining moments
lessons.subtitle: A captain makes his mark for club and country.

story.title: The title-day opener
story.body: Totti scored first in the decisive match against Parma as Roma secured the 2000-01 title.

story.title: A century of league goals
story.body: Totti reached his hundredth Serie A goal against Inter in October 2004. He later recovered from a serious injury to join Italy’s World Cup squad and convert a vital knockout-round penalty.

facts.label: Roma title-day opponent
facts.prompt: Against which club did Totti open the scoring in Roma’s 17 June 2001 title-clinching match?
facts.scope: The final day of the 2000-01 Serie A season, when Roma secured the Scudetto.
facts.evidence: The profile says Totti opened the scoring in the decisive game against Parma on 17 June 2001.

facts.label: World Cup penalty opponent
facts.prompt: Against which national team did Totti score a crucial penalty in the 2006 World Cup round of 16?
facts.scope: Italy’s 2006 World Cup round-of-16 match on its route to the final.
facts.evidence: The profile identifies Totti’s crucial Round of 16 penalty as being against Australia.

facts.label: Opponent for Totti’s hundredth Serie A goal
facts.prompt: Against which club did Totti score his hundredth Serie A goal on 3 October 2004?
facts.scope: Totti’s hundredth Serie A goal, 3 October 2004.
facts.evidence: The Hall of Fame biography identifies Inter as the opponent for his hundredth Serie A goal.

lessons.title: Totti’s Roma record book
lessons.subtitle: Separate Totti’s league records from his totals across competitions.

story.title: Unmatched longevity
story.body: Totti’s final competitive Roma appearance came in May 2017, after a 24-year first-team career.

story.title: A prolific scorer
story.body: His club Hall of Fame profile lists totals across Serie A, domestic cups and European competitions.

facts.label: Roma appearances
facts.prompt: How many competitive appearances did Totti make for Roma?
facts.scope: Totti’s final all-competition Roma total in the club Hall of Fame profile.
facts.evidence: The profile’s competition table gives the total as 786 appearances.

facts.label: Roma goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Totti score for Roma in all competitions?
facts.scope: Totti’s final all-competition Roma total in the club Hall of Fame profile.
facts.evidence: The profile’s competition table totals his goals at 307.

facts.label: Serie A goals
facts.prompt: How many Serie A goals did Totti score for Roma?
facts.scope: His Serie A scoring total for Roma, listed in the Hall of Fame competition table.
facts.evidence: The profile lists 619 Serie A appearances and 250 goals.

lessons.title: Totti’s club and individual honours
lessons.subtitle: Explore team trophies and an individual scoring award.

story.title: Two cup competitions
story.body: Totti lifted the Coppa Italia twice and the Italian Super Cup twice with Roma.

story.title: An individual prize
story.body: In 2006-07, he finished as Serie A’s top scorer and won the European Golden Shoe.

facts.label: Roma Coppa Italia titles
facts.prompt: How many Coppa Italia titles did Totti win with Roma?
facts.scope: Roma team honours listed in the club Hall of Fame article.
facts.evidence: The club Hall of Fame account lists two Coppa Italia titles for Totti.

facts.label: Roma Italian Super Cups
facts.prompt: How many Italian Super Cup titles did Totti win with Roma?
facts.scope: Roma team honours listed in the club Hall of Fame article.
facts.evidence: The club Hall of Fame account lists two Italian Super Cups for Totti.

facts.label: European Golden Shoe season
facts.prompt: In which season did Totti win the European Golden Shoe?
facts.scope: The European Golden Shoe award season listed in the club Hall of Fame article.
facts.evidence: The article identifies the European Golden Shoe as his 2006-07 individual accolade.

lessons.title: A Roma academy graduate
lessons.subtitle: Follow De Rossi from the academy to his last playing chapter.

story.title: A boyhood club
story.body: The Rome-born academy graduate joined the club he supported as a teenager in 2000.

story.title: From debut to departure
story.body: He debuted in the Champions League in October 2001 and later spent the final six months of his playing career with Boca Juniors.

facts.label: Joined Roma year
facts.prompt: In what year did De Rossi join the club he supported as a teenager?
facts.scope: The year De Rossi joined Roma before making his first-team debut.
facts.evidence: The club’s 2019 announcement says he joined Roma in 2000.

facts.label: First-team debut opponent
facts.prompt: Against which club did De Rossi make his Roma first-team debut on 30 October 2001?
facts.scope: The Champions League group-stage debut at the Stadio Olimpico.
facts.evidence: The official debut retrospective identifies Anderlecht as the opponent.

facts.label: Final playing club
facts.prompt: At which club did De Rossi finish his professional playing career after Roma?
facts.scope: The six-month final playing spell referenced in De Rossi’s 2020 retirement announcement.
facts.evidence: The retirement announcement says De Rossi ended his career after a six-month spell with Argentine side Boca Juniors.

lessons.title: Leadership and a night in Rome
lessons.subtitle: Captaincy and a remarkable European comeback.

story.title: The armband
story.body: He captained Roma for the first time from kick-off against Middlesbrough in March 2006.

story.title: A famous comeback
story.body: In 2018, he scored Roma’s second goal as the team overturned Barcelona’s 4-1 first-leg lead.

facts.label: First captaincy date
facts.prompt: On what date did De Rossi first captain Roma from kick-off?
facts.scope: The UEFA Cup last-16 second leg against Middlesbrough.
facts.evidence: The debut retrospective dates his first captaincy to 15 March 2006.

facts.label: Minute of De Rossi’s comeback penalty
facts.prompt: In which minute did De Rossi score his penalty in Roma’s 2018 Champions League comeback against Barcelona?
facts.scope: Roma–Barcelona second leg, 10 April 2018; minute listed in the official match report.
facts.evidence: The club’s event log lists De Rossi’s penalty at minute 58.

facts.label: Roma-Barcelona second-leg score
facts.prompt: What was Roma’s score against Barcelona in the 10 April 2018 Champions League second leg?
facts.scope: Second leg only; Roma drew 4-4 on aggregate and advanced on away goals.
facts.evidence: The match report headline and final match line record Roma 3-0 Barcelona; aggregate and away-goal outcome are stated separately.

lessons.title: A Roma mainstay in the numbers
lessons.subtitle: Explore De Rossi’s appearances, goals and leadership record.

story.title: A long service
story.body: Across 18 years, De Rossi made more than six hundred appearances for Roma.

story.title: Midfielder and captain
story.body: His club retrospective records goals and captaincy totals alongside appearances.

facts.label: Roma appearances
facts.prompt: How many appearances did De Rossi make for Roma in all competitions?
facts.scope: His completed Roma total, as listed in the club’s 2020 career retrospective.
facts.evidence: The retirement announcement says he made 616 appearances for Roma.

facts.label: Roma goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did De Rossi score for Roma in all competitions?
facts.scope: His Roma goal total across competitions.
facts.evidence: The club’s debut retrospective states 616 appearances and 63 goals; the 2019 departure article confirms 63 goals.

facts.label: Roma matches as captain
facts.prompt: How many times did De Rossi captain Roma?
facts.scope: De Rossi’s Roma captaincy total, in the club’s 2020 debut retrospective.
facts.evidence: The article gives 207 as the number of Roma appearances as captain.

lessons.title: De Rossi’s international and club honours
lessons.subtitle: Club trophies and international success across De Rossi’s career.

story.title: A world champion
story.body: De Rossi played in the 2006 World Cup final as Italy won the tournament.

story.title: Roma silverware
story.body: His Roma honours included consecutive Coppa Italia titles and a 2007 Supercoppa.

facts.label: World Cup year
facts.prompt: In what year did De Rossi win the FIFA World Cup with Italy?
facts.scope: His international senior-team World Cup win.
facts.evidence: The club states De Rossi was part of Italy’s 2006 World Cup-winning side and played in the final.

facts.label: Roma Coppa Italia titles
facts.prompt: How many Coppa Italia titles did De Rossi win with Roma?
facts.scope: Roma honours through his departure in 2019.
facts.evidence: The 2019 announcement lists Coppa Italia wins in 2007 and 2008.

facts.label: Roma Supercoppa wins
facts.prompt: How many Supercoppa titles did De Rossi win with Roma?
facts.scope: Roma honours through his departure in 2019.
facts.evidence: The club lists one Supercoppa title, won in 2007.
